claims: The ZPL compiler returns a value equal to expression evaluation together with lower and upper payoff bounds.
Core payoff combinators preserve certified bounds compositionally.
Floor and ceil fixed-point runtime decoding stay within a conservative one-tick expansion of the real-valued certified interval.
Posted collateral covering the mode-expanded interval prevents bilateral default for single-leg and finite portfolio settlements.
Two-party fixed-point settlement deltas conserve exactly when represented as holder delta plus negated writer delta.
Finite FIRE budget certificates compose additively and preserve the fail-closed spend rule spend <= verifiedValue + explicitBudget.
A unified FIRE portfolio receipt packages bilateral solvency and exact conservation for compiled ZPL portfolios.
proof_method: structural compiler soundness over a small payoff expression language

checker_commands.command: cd lean-mathlib && lake build Proofs.ZenoPayoffLanguage Proofs.ZPLPayoffCombinators Proofs.ZenoPayoffFixedPointBridge Proofs.ZenoPayoffPortfolioFixedPointBridge Proofs.FIREBudgetSafety Proofs.FIREUnified

checker_commands.result: passed with pre-existing linter warnings in unrelated proof files

boundaries: This package proves a proof-level model, not direct bytecode or deployed smart-contract verification.
The fixed-point bridge assumes a positive scale and uses a one-tick conservative expansion around real payoff bounds.
Solvency conclusions require posted collateral to cover the certified lower and upper interval selected by the rounding mode.
The proofs certify payoff bounds, collateral no-default, conservation, and budget caps; they do not prove oracle validity, market completeness, fair pricing, or legal/regulatory compliance.
Runtime integration still needs executable conformance tests or a compiler/extraction proof tying deployed code to these Lean definitions.
